result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_reverse_edges_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add reverse edges for all selected edges (directed graphs only). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L17084-L17183){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_reverse_edges_ws(**edge_attributes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Add reverse edges for the selection](/assets/graphs/add-reverse-edges-ws.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a directed six-node graph with edges B→C and D→E selected in the accent color. Right: each selected edge gains a reverse partner, C→B and E→D, drawn in the accent color; the original edges stay, so those pairs now point both ways." width="100%"} For each selected edge (A->B), adds the reverse edge (B->A) if it doesn't already exist. Useful for making directed graphs bidirectional or adding reciprocal relationships. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [**edge_attributes]{.doc-parameter-name} : Optional attributes to set on the newly created reverse edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#2f8b0ddd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label='A') .add_node(label='B') .add_edge(source='A', target='B', weight=1.0) ) # Add reverse edge edge_ids = list(graph.get_edge_ids()) ( graph .select_edges_by_id([edge_ids[0]]) .add_reverse_edges_ws(weight=1.0) ) # Returns 2 (A->B and B->A) graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Make selected edges bidirectional -- here, only the heavier "A->B" edge gets a reverse, since "B->C" falls below the weight threshold: ::: {#7fc7ead6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label='A') .add_node(label='B') .add_node(label='C') .add_edge(source='A', target='B', weight=10.0) .add_edge(source='B', target='C', weight=3.0) ) ( graph .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight is not None and e.weight > 5.0) .add_reverse_edges_ws() ) graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: :::
